data.title: Celsius jumps on report Rockstar Energy founder takes stake, wants to be CEO (update)
data.description:
Update 1:20pm: Adds Celsius response.

Celsius Holdings (CELH) soared 12% after a report that Rockstar Energy founder  Russ Savage has taken a stake and wants to change management after the energy drink maker's earnings miss on Thursday.

The billionaire founder of Rockstar, who sold the company to PepsiCo in 2020 for $3.85 billion, controls more than 12 million Celsius (CELH) shares, he told CNBC on Friday. 

While Savage has been talking quietly to Celsius (CELH) about changing its cost structure and marketing for over a year, he now believes new leadership is needed. 

“The CEO, the COO, the brand manager, and the marketing manager all need to be fired,” Savage, who now has a 4.7% stake in Celsius (CELH), told the business network.

He said he would like to take over as CEO to resolve the problems at the energy drink maker.  Celsius last August agreed to acquire the U.S. and Canadian rights to the Rockstar Energy brand from PepsiCo (PEP).

“I’m publicly volunteering to do it,” Savage told CNBC. “The CEO has lost credibility with the investment community.”

A Celsius spokesperson responded to the comments in an emailed statement to Seeking Alpha.

"We welcome ideas that are potentially value-creating from all Celsius Holdings shareholders," the spokesperson said in the statement. "Yesterday, Celsius Holdings reported record second quarter financial results, reflecting continued demand and resilience across our consumer base. We remain focused on executing our total energy portfolio strategy to drive durable, long-term growth. Members of our Board and management team have engaged with Russ Savage many times over the past several years."

The comments come after Celsius (CELH) shares plunged 18% on Thursday after reporting Q2 revenue that was short of analysts' estimates.

data.title: Scripps targets $100M annual run-rate savings by year-end as it forecasts $225M-$250M in political ads
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: E.W. Scripps (SSP) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "We're very pleased that the commission has made the decision in the direction of further leveling the playing field in the media business by finally addressing some of the arcane rules that have significantly impaired the broadcast industry." (President, CEO & Director Adam Symson)
  • "We're targeting $125 million to $150 million in incremental enterprise EBITDA by 2028. And we now expect to have executed on $100 million in annual run rate savings by the end of this year." (Executive VP & CFO Jason Combs)
  • "During the second quarter, we made further gains in our Scripps Sports strategy, signing our first NBA agreement with the Detroit Pistons in our Local Media division." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "We completed the last of 3 major distribution agreements, covering the majority of our pay TV subscriber households renewing this year." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "This week, we notified 268 employees that their jobs would be eliminated." (President, CEO & Director Symson)
  • "That's one of the reasons why I've asked Dean Littleton to oversee the Networks business as well as Local Media in his new role as President of Media." (President, CEO & Director Symson)

Outlook

  • "For the third quarter, on an adjusted combined or same-station basis, we expect Local Media division revenue to be up about 20%." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "We expect core advertising to be down low double digits, in line with the core revenue decline in the third quarter of the 2022 midterms." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "We expect our political advertising revenue for the full year to reach a range of $225 million to $250 million." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "We now expect full year gross distribution revenue to be down in the low single-digit percent range, but net distribution revenue to be up in the mid- to high single digits." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "For the third quarter, we expect Scripps Networks division revenue to be down in the mid-teens percent range" and "we expect Scripps Networks expenses to be up in the low single digits." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • Analysts’ estimates were provided for revenue only, but the estimates JSON did not include valid fiscal quarter labeling (Q1–Q4) and no EPS estimates; no comparison is included.

Financial Results

  • "During the second quarter, our Local Media division revenue was $317 million" and "Local Media segment profit was $56 million." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "Scripps Networks revenue was $172 million" and "Scripps Networks' Q2 segment profit was $26 million." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "For the second quarter, the company is reporting a loss of $12.68 per share" and "we reported a $1.1 billion noncash goodwill and other intangible asset impairment charge for the Scripps Networks business." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "The quarter also included $36 million in restructuring costs" and "a $9 million gain from our swaps with Gray Media." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "We ended the quarter with $13 million in cash" and "Net debt was $2.2 billion as defined in our credit agreement." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • "Net leverage at the end of the quarter was 4.9x as compared to 4.4x at the end of Q1 when calculated on the same basis." (Executive VP & CFO Combs)

Q&A

  • Daniel Kurnos, The Benchmark Company, LLC: asked if Q3 core is pacing down low double digits; Executive VP & CFO Combs: "Yes, low doubles in Q3, driven by the political crowd you would expect." President, CEO & Director Symson added: "the onset of the NBA and NHL seasons will just start in third quarter and then really come into their own in fourth quarter."
  • Daniel Kurnos, The Benchmark Company, LLC: asked about 2027 retrans trajectory; Executive VP & CFO Combs: "We're not going to give any guidance now" and later corrected subs resetting: "That's actually in 2028. Next year is only 5%."
  • Daniel Kurnos, The Benchmark Company, LLC: pressed on Nielsen methodology and local impact; President, CEO & Director Symson: "our performance softness, I'd attribute about 50% of that to the sudden change in Nielsen" and "None of the upside of a fix is baked into our guide."
  • Craig Huber, Huber Research Partners, LLC: asked whether the company might be sold; President, CEO & Director Symson: "I don't speak for our controlling shareholder" and "we believe greater scale nationally and greater depth in market are helpful for our assets to perform their very best."
  • Craig Huber, Huber Research Partners, LLC: asked about cost to achieve transformation savings; Executive VP & CFO Combs: "we had guided to $40 million to $50 million in cash restructuring costs" and for the quarter "of the $36 million in restructuring... about $12 million of that is actually cash... about $9 million is accrued... roughly $15 million... noncash."
  • Steven Cahall, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: asked about Networks margin path; Executive VP & CFO Combs: "We continue to believe that this business should be closer to 30% margin" and "we intend to chart the path forward to see a similar rebound."
  • Steven Cahall, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: asked about monetizing spectrum and auctions; President, CEO & Director Symson: "we're sitting on a goldmine of spectrum" and "when there is an opportunity to monetize our spectrum, either through an incentive auction... maybe as early as 2028... we will take full advantage."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative and pressing on Nielsen disruption, visibility into distribution economics, and strategic alternatives, including the direct question on selling the company.
  • Management: slightly negative on near-term results but confident on controllable actions; President, CEO & Director Symson said, "Our financial performance for the quarter didn't meet my expectations" while also emphasizing "permanent benefits" from transformation and stating, "The blackouts are now behind us."
  • Versus last quarter: management tone shifted from Q1’s "strong momentum" framing to Q2’s acknowledgment of misses and impairment drivers, while analyst focus tightened on Nielsen quantification, leverage trajectory, and the feasibility/timing of transformation benefits.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Transformation timing accelerated: Q1 described an "annualized run rate of about $75 million as we move into next year" (Executive VP & CFO Combs), while Q2 raised the year-end expectation to "$100 million" (Executive VP & CFO Combs).
  • Networks pressure intensified: Q1 guided Networks revenue down about 10% with "external measurement pressure from Nielsen" (Executive VP & CFO Combs), while Q2 included a $1.1B impairment and guidance for revenue down in the mid-teens percent range.
  • Distribution narrative moved from an active Comcast impasse in Q1 to Q2 stating the company "completed the last of 3 major distribution agreements" (Executive VP & CFO Combs), with management describing renewed subs and improved longer-term economics.
  • Leadership/actions expanded: Q2 added the appointment of Dean Littleton as President of Media and disclosed workforce reductions, items not presented with specific headcount figures in Q1.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Sudden changes to Nielsen's measurement methodology" and "continued declines in linear viewing" were cited as key headwinds. (President, CEO & Director Symson)
  • "Broader economic uncertainty" and a "softer direct response advertising market" were identified as revenue pressures, alongside lingering effects from carriage blackouts. (Executive VP & CFO Combs)
  • Mitigation centered on distribution renegotiations, sports-driven inventory, and transformation-led cost actions; management emphasized, "None of the upside of a fix is baked into our guide." (President, CEO & Director Symson)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q2 as a quarter of operational progress but weaker reported performance, anchored by a $1.1B Networks impairment, Nielsen-driven measurement disruption, and blackout-related distribution impacts. The company emphasized accelerated transformation execution to reach a $100M annual run-rate savings by year-end, expanded sports rights (including its first NBA deal), completed major distribution renewals, and maintained a full-year political advertising outlook of $225M–$250M, while reorganizing oversight of Networks under a new President of Media and implementing workforce reductions to support the transformation plan.

data.title: Mach outlines plan to return leverage to 1x by end of 2027 while distributing $0.36 per unit
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Mach Natural Resources (MNR) Q2 2026

Management View

  • CEO Tom Ward framed the quarter around Mach’s “4 strategic pillars,” emphasizing a “reinvestment rate of less than 50% of our operating cash flow,” a push to reduce leverage, and maximizing unitholder payouts, while noting the partnership “strategically moved leverage above our goal of 1x debt to EBITDA” to pursue acquisitions and now aims to return to target.

  • Ward laid out multiple deleveraging levers and timing: “We also have an at-the-market equity program to place $100 million of equity at prices that do not disturb trading.” He added, “Our team is dedicated to meet our goal before the end of 2027.”

  • Ward highlighted drilling flexibility and a near-term oil tilt tied to capital discipline: “The completion phase of this year's drilling has been delayed until next year in order to stay within our internally mandated annual CapEx of 50% of operating cash flow.” He also said, “Given that restraint, it's more valuable for us to drill for oil rates of return versus natural gas in the last half of this year.”

  • CFO Kevin White provided the quarter’s operational and cash-return headline: “In the quarter, we generated $60 million of cash available for distribution, resulting in a distribution of $0.36 per unit, which will be paid on August 31 to holders of record on August 17.”

  • Senior executive Richard Hughes attributed a key cost lever in the San Juan program to execution and vendors: “we're optimizing our drilling performance and being able to get reduced overall days drilling is the main thing we've been able to change. bringing some new vendors in, obviously, has helped reduce costs as well.”

Outlook

  • Management did not provide formal EPS or revenue guidance in the prepared remarks or Q&A; the discussion centered on capital pacing, commodity-driven drilling choices, and leverage targets.

  • Ward positioned the company’s medium-term flexibility around the San Juan/Mancos: “by the time the contract amortizes in 2030, we'll have strategic optionality for our 350 million cubic feet of natural gas that can be held flat by drilling only 5 net wells per year.” He added, “If we choose to increase activity to 10 net wells per year, we could grow Mach's net production to more than 500 million cubic feet of gas per day.”

  • On Mancos economics, Ward said cost-down is central to future activity levels: “we expect the ongoing program to be in the $13 million range for a completed well.”

Financial Results

  • White reported Q2 production of 149,000 BOE per day (15% oil, 69% natural gas, 16% NGLs) and average realized prices of $95.40 per barrel of oil, $1.93 per Mcf of gas, and $28.99 per barrel of NGLs.

  • White reported $360 million of total oil and gas revenues, and said “Total revenues, including our hedges and midstream activities totaled $406 million,” with adjusted EBITDA of $182 million and operating cash flow of $154 million.

  • On costs and liquidity, White said lease operating expense was $98 million ($7.21 per BOE) and cash G&A was about $7 million ($0.54 per BOE). He added, “We ended the quarter with $41 million in cash and $270 million of availability under the credit facility.”

  • Capital intensity moved higher in Q2 versus Mach’s target band: White said development CapEx was $97 million, “63% of operating cash flow,” while adding, “Year-to-date, our development CapEx is right on top of 50% of our year-to-date operating cash flow.”

Q&A

  • Neal Dingmann, William Blair: asked about near-term D&C focus and Oswego economics; CEO Ward answered, “The ongoing drilling program that we have through Q4 of this year is to keep an Oswego rig running,” and added, “we have basically an 85% rate of return at $75 oil.”

  • Neal Dingmann, William Blair: asked about reinvestment rate and cash deployment; CFO White said, “we were right on top of 50% year-to-date,” and CEO Ward added, “the operating cash flow drives what our CapEx is.”

  • Charles Meade, Johnson Rice: asked what gas price is needed to complete Mancos wells; CEO Ward replied, “if prices continued to be under $3, I think it would be difficult to have any gas program in the U.S. working,” and said the decision depends on whether “the Mancos can compete against our oil reservoirs.”

  • Michael Scialla, Stephens: asked about Clearfork plans and competitiveness; CEO Ward said, “we don't have it in our drilling schedule yet,” adding the Clearfork showed “a 53% rate of return compared to the Oswego in the 80s.”

  • Michael Scialla, Stephens: asked if distributions or strategy may change to reduce leverage; CEO Ward said, “we want to be at 1x leverage,” and listed options including, “we can always cut our distribution some,” while noting deal markets: “there's just a lot of capital chasing a few deals right now.”

  • Derrick Whitfield, Texas Capital: asked about 2027 oil vs. gas activity and San Juan basis; CEO Ward said, “Yes, I think that's fair” on oil-first sequencing, and warned, “I'm scared of San Juan basis right now,” while citing longer-term relief via “The GreenView pipeline.”

  • Jeffrey Grampp, Northland: asked about Mancos cost reductions and oil growth; CEO Ward cited service and design choices and said, “our production -- projection into '27 is basically keeping it flat.”

  • Timothy Rezvan, KeyBanc: asked about asset sales/farms to accelerate deleveraging; CEO Ward said, “selling assets are difficult because you're losing cash flow,” and concluded, “selling away your assets to me is not as efficient as if we were to cut a distribution.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing on leverage and 2027 activity assumptions, with repeated probing on how Mach plans to move from “around 1.4x at year-end” toward the 1x target and what that implies for CAD and distributions.

  • Management tone was confident on flexibility and long-term gas optionality but more cautious on near-term gas/basis and balance sheet timing; Ward used direct risk language (“I'm scared of San Juan basis right now”) while reiterating conviction in process (“the cash flow dictates our pace of CapEx”).

  • Versus the prior quarter, management sounded more urgent on deleveraging execution (“it's time for us to get started here soon”), while Q1 emphasized that leverage could “naturally” improve with commodity prices; analysts similarly shifted from drilling-plan mechanics toward more explicit questions on balance sheet actions.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q2 distribution was $0.36 per unit vs. $0.64 per unit in Q1, alongside lower cash available for distribution ($60 million in Q2 vs. $107 million in Q1) and a higher quarterly development CapEx burden (63% of operating cash flow in Q2 vs. 40% of operating cash flow after interest in Q1).

  • Strategic messaging remained anchored to sub-50% reinvestment and flexibility, but Q2 increased emphasis on managing leverage back to 1x, including explicit tools (the $100 million ATM) and acknowledgment that leverage “hasn't moved down yet.”

  • Analyst focus broadened from Q1 questions on production mix and service inflation to Q2 questions on balance sheet actions (asset sales, payout adjustments) and San Juan basis risk.

Risks and Concerns

  • Ward highlighted near-term natural gas uncertainty and basis volatility as key constraints on Mancos capital timing: “we wouldn't spend any CapEx if prices continued to be under $3,” and separately, “I'm scared of San Juan basis right now.”

  • Leverage remained a stated concern, with Ward describing projected year-end leverage and the need to act: “we recognize that we are running a company today that at today's prices, looking at the end of the year is 1.4x levered, and we want to be at 1x leverage.”

  • Ward cited competitive deal dynamics as a hurdle to equity-funded acquisitions that could delever: “there's just a lot of capital chasing a few deals right now.”

Final Takeaway

Management reiterated Mach’s variable, cash-flow-driven capital program and highlighted a Q2 distribution of $0.36 per unit alongside a renewed push to reduce leverage from a projected 1.4x at year-end back to the 1x target before the end of 2027, using tools such as a $100 million ATM and, if needed, a lower distribution. The call’s core operational debate centered on timing Mancos completions amid sub-$3 gas and volatile San Juan basis, while emphasizing that oil-weighted drilling (especially Oswego) remains the highest-return outlet for capital under the partnership’s sub-50% reinvestment framework.

data.title: Take-Two reiterates FY2027 net bookings $8B-$8.2B with GTA VI set for Nov. 19 release
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) Q1 fiscal 2027

Management view

  • “Fiscal 2027 is off to an excellent start,” said (Executive Chairman & CEO Strauss Zelnick), as Take-Two reported first-quarter net bookings of approximately $1.39 billion and reiterated full-year net bookings of $8 billion to $8.2 billion, which he said reflects “our high degree of confidence around the November 19 release of Grand Theft Auto VI.”
  • Zelnick highlighted strength in key franchises: “We delivered first quarter net bookings of approximately $1.39 billion… primarily due to the outperformance of NBA 2K and the Grand Theft Auto series,” and added that GTA VI had “an exceptional start to preorders.”
  • (President Karl Slatoff) outlined near-term release timing and live-ops cadence, including NBA 2K27 launching September 4 and ongoing content for GTA Online, Borderlands 4, Mafia: The Old Country, and WWE 2K26.
  • (Chief Financial Officer Lainie Goldstein) said, “We delivered first quarter net bookings of $1.39 billion, which was slightly above our guidance range of $1.32 billion to $1.37 billion,” citing better-than-expected NBA 2K and GTA performance, while noting cost of revenue included “a $43 million impairment charge related to the decision not to proceed with an unannounced title from a third-party developer.”

Outlook

  • Management reiterated FY2027 net bookings of $8 billion to $8.2 billion, with Goldstein adding it “represents approximately 20% growth over fiscal 2026 at the midpoint,” and saying Take-Two continues to expect recurrent consumer spending to be in line with fiscal 2026 and to represent 64% of net bookings.
  • Goldstein updated the expected label mix for FY2027 net bookings to roughly 37% Rockstar Games, 34% Zynga, and 29% 2K, and said capex is now planned at approximately $290 million, “up from our prior forecast due to a planned real estate purchase.”
  • For fiscal Q2, Goldstein guided net bookings to $1.62 billion to $1.67 billion, GAAP net revenue to $1.42 billion to $1.47 billion, and said management-basis operating expenses are expected to decline by approximately 5% year-over-year as last year included significant marketing for Borderlands 4.
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s initial FY2027 framework, management kept the FY net bookings range unchanged while raising planned capex (previously approximately $200 million) and slightly reducing expected management-basis opex growth (now approximately 7% year-over-year vs. prior forecast of approximately 8%).

Financial results

  • Goldstein reported GAAP net revenue increased 2% to $1.5 billion; cost of revenue rose 17% to $651 million (including the $43 million impairment); and operating expenses were flat at $918 million.
  • She added recurrent consumer spending declined 1% and accounted for 84% of net bookings, with NBA 2K recurrent consumer spending up 7%, the Grand Theft Auto series up 3%, and mobile down 7%.

Q&A

  • Douglas Creutz, TD Cowen: asked about a mobile market slowdown; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said, “No, it’s really not what we’re seeing,” adding there is “a bit of pressure on user acquisition” but “we don’t feel like the consumer is pulling back at all.”
  • Andrew Marok, Raymond James: asked why the GTA VI “extended look” is launching with Netflix; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) called it “a first-of-its-kind partnership with Netflix,” and said it will be on YouTube via Rockstar’s channel “6 hours after the initial launch.”
  • Brian Pitz, BMO: asked about GTA VI pricing vs. NBA 2K27; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said, “Our goal is not to maximize price,” emphasizing value delivery and that pricing hasn’t kept pace with inflation.
  • Eric Handler, ROTH: asked about exclusivity economics with Netflix; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) declined to discuss terms, saying he “wouldn’t normally give detail” on the arrangement.
  • Eric Handler, ROTH: asked about rising hardware costs delaying consoles; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said it is “not a good thing,” but added Take-Two doesn’t see it as “a headwind,” and said, “I think we’ll be in commercial streaming mode within 3 years.”
  • Colin Sebastian, Baird: asked about NBA 2K growth drivers and AI use; (President Slatoff) said there remains “a huge amount of growth potential,” and (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said AI tools “are not going to replace anyone,” adding the company is “dyed-in-the-wool adopters of new technology.”
  • Christopher Schoell, UBS: asked about international expansion and M&A criteria; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) described underpenetration in markets such as India and Africa and said, “my goal is that in the next 10 years, we flip the percentage of our revenue that comes from the U.S. and international markets,” and said M&A criteria include buying IP/teams/tools and being “immediately accretive to EBITDA and to GAAP earnings.”
  • Alec Brondolo, Wells Fargo: asked about GTA VI SKU structure and preorder incrementality; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said, “we haven’t sold one unit yet. You can cancel a preorder,” and added, “we’re… cautiously optimistic.”
  • Matthew Cost, Morgan Stanley: asked about a shift away from physical discs and Zynga direct payments; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said the business is “well over 90% digitally distributed,” and that direct-to-consumer “has had a material effect positive on our margins in the Mobile business.”
  • Jason Bazinet, Citi: asked how to “dimensionalize” preorders; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said preorders are “unprecedented and astonishing,” but “we genuinely don’t know” how they translate into sales.
  • Taebin Song, Wolfe: asked about advertising beyond mobile; (Executive Chairman & CEO Zelnick) said advertising is growing in mobile to help monetize broader audiences, while on console it should be limited unless “endemic to the title.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing around mobile softness, preorder sustainability, hardware cycle risk, and monetization topics; questions included “slowdown in the Mobile market,” whether preorders are being “pulled forward,” and concerns that next-gen consoles may be delayed.
  • Management tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in Q&A on GTA VI demand translation; Zelnick said, “we’re sort of allergic to victory laps,” and emphasized uncertainty despite calling preorders “unprecedented.”
  • Versus the prior quarter, management kept a similar confidence posture on FY2027 scale uplift tied to GTA VI, but Q&A focus shifted from announcing the FY outlook to execution details: pricing structure, marketing distribution via Netflix, and interpreting preorder signals.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The FY2027 net bookings range remained $8 billion to $8.2 billion, while FY capex increased to approximately $290 million (previously approximately $200 million) due to “a planned real estate purchase,” and management-basis opex growth expectation eased to approximately 7% (from approximately 8%).
  • Current-quarter narrative leaned more heavily on GTA VI commercialization specifics (pricing at $80, SKU mix, Netflix trailer partnership, preorder caveats) than the prior quarter, which centered on initial FY2027 setup and the multi-year pipeline framing.

Risks and concerns

  • Goldstein disclosed a $43 million impairment tied to discontinuing an unannounced third-party title, indicating portfolio churn risk.
  • Zelnick flagged pressure in mobile user acquisition economics: “there’s a bit of pressure on user acquisition,” and later described competitor overspending as potentially “crowd[ing] us out of the market.”
  • Management repeatedly emphasized preorder uncertainty and cancellation risk: “You can cancel a preorder,” and said guidance was unchanged because “we haven’t sold one unit yet.”

Final takeaway

Take-Two management framed Q1 as an “excellent start” driven by NBA 2K and GTA, reiterated FY2027 net bookings of $8 billion to $8.2 billion anchored by the November 19 GTA VI release, and highlighted unprecedented preorder levels while cautioning that preorders may not translate cleanly into launch sales. The company raised planned FY capex due to a real estate purchase, maintained expectations for more than $1 billion in operating cash flow, and emphasized ongoing scale opportunities from live services, direct-to-consumer expansion in mobile, international growth initiatives, and selective accretive M&A.

data.title: NRx Pharma rises as FDA completes initial review of ketamine product
data.description:
Shares of NRx Pharmaceuticals (NRXP) rose on Friday after the company announced that the FDA didn't identify any major deficiencies as part of an initial review of its marketing application for its preservative-free ketamine product.

The regulator didn’t identify any drug-related review matters during the first-cycle review of its ANDA, the company said, adding it is not required to submit any new clinical or drug-related findings to prove the product’s safety and efficacy.

However, the FDA questioned whether the luer lock tip of the medication vial would properly operate when attached to a syringe, which the regulator classified as a major deficiency. 

However, following a clarification meeting with the FDA on Aug. 6, NRx Pharma (NRXP) cites a substantially de-risked path to approval, noting that three ANDA-approved products currently on the market use the luer-lock medication vial.

“We are encouraged by FDA’s commitment at the meeting to review this remaining information in the shortest-possible review cycle and remain focused on advancing our ANDA toward approval and commercialization,” CEO Jonathan Javitt remarked.

data.title: Lyft's results leave analysts split over AV threat, pricing
data.description:
Lyft (LYFT) shares reached their highest level in 6 months and pierced the 200-day moving average on another quarter of better-than-expected quarterly results and record-setting ride/rider metrics.

“We achieved an all-time high of over 30 million active riders, proving that rideshare is embedded in people’s everyday lives,” noted Lyft CEO David Risher.

The company achieved double-digit gross bookings, active riders, and total revenue, underscoring the company’s successful efforts to expand into new markets and engage new partners.

For the current quarter, Lyft (LYFT) expects gross bookings to increase another 15% to 19% to a range that straddles the consensus estimate of $5.58B estimates.

RBC Capital’s Brad Erickson: We like the favorable mix shift the company is leaning into with partner rides now 30% of total, other higher-value modes, airport rides, etc. We continue to detect very low confidence in Lyft and negativity around ride-hailing in general, given Waymo is poised to enter double digits in more cities in the U.S. With that said, the ride-hail market continues to demonstrate secular growth with Lyft rationally keeping pace, which we’d view as not appreciated in the shares. Outperform, $20 price target (was $18).

BofA Securities’ Justin Post: The AV debate, not results, will be the top driver of the stock price. We have preferred Uber as we think Uber’s balance sheet and scale make the company better positioned to integrate [autonomous vehicles]. However, we acknowledge that Lyft could make a very interesting AV partner for an Uber competitor. Underperform, $18 price target (was $17).

Wells Fargo’s Ken Gawrelski: Print and guide both modestly ahead of expectations but would prefer a mix of greater volumes and less price. We are concerned about higher headline prices and a steady diet of consumer incentives to stimulate demand. Equal Weight, $19 price target (was $18).

Oppenheimer’s Chad Larkin: Despite a strong quarter, the Q3 outlook is largely in line with the street and therefore not enough to impact investor sentiment. However, with results no longer missing street estimates, shares will likely move higher as investors exit short positions, particularly with shares trading 6x 2027 EBITDA. Outperform, $20 price target.

data.title: Volkswagen controlling shareholders urge faster overhaul as Chinese rivals intensify pressure
data.description:
Volkswagen's (VWAGY) controlling shareholders have urged the German automaker to speed up its restructuring plans, warning that delays could undermine its ability to compete with Chinese carmakers, CNBC reported on Friday.

"The decisions that Volkswagen makes now will determine its future," Hans Dieter Pötsch, chairman of Porsche SE's management board, said, describing Volkswagen (VWAGY) as being at a 'historic crossroads." He said the company should focus on measures needed to strengthen its long-term competitiveness.

Volkswagen (VWAGY) has said it is considering cutting up to 100,000 jobs as it seeks to address falling profitability, rising tariff costs, and mounting competition from Chinese automakers.

Johannes Lattwein, Porsche SE's board member responsible for finance and IT, said it was “imperative” for Volkswagen (VWAGY) to reduce excess capacity, lower costs, and strengthen decision-making and execution. He added that Porsche SE supported Volkswagen's (VWAGY) management and that "every option must be considered" to improve the group's competitive position.

A Volkswagen (VWAGY) spokesperson said Porsche SE's comments were consistent with the automaker's restructuring plans and reinforced the urgency of carrying them out.

Chief Executive Oliver Blume has said Volkswagen (VWAGY) has already begun implementing its turnaround strategy, while Chief Financial Officer Arno Antlitz said the company's priority is to improve productivity, lower costs, and increase factory utilization rather than pursue job cuts or plant closures for their own sake.

data.title: Chesapeake outlines $1.2B Florida Energy Pathway project targeting 2030 in-service, while lifting 2026 capex to $550M-$600M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (CPK) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "Our growth trajectory has continued through the second quarter as we reported a 5% increase in adjusted net income, driving an 8% increase in adjusted earnings per share through the first six months of this year," said (President, CEO & Chairman Jeffrey Householder), adding, "In the second quarter, we generated an incremental $10 million of margin" and "invested $140 million of capital in the second quarter" with "total year-to-date investment" of "$262 million."
  • "We just announced" the Florida Energy Pathway Project (FEP) and described it as "a 97-mile intrastate natural gas transmission infrastructure project" and "the largest single project in our company's history," representing "total investment of approximately $1.2 billion," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder). He said Peninsula Pipeline "will fund and own at least 51%" and that FEP is "expected to be in service in 2030" and "anchored by multiple investment-grade shippers who've committed to nearly 250,000 dekatherms per day of capacity."
  • "We're increasing our full year 2026 capital guidance by $100 million, resulting in an updated range of $550 million to $600 million," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder), citing "initial spending for FEP" and "increases in regulated distribution and infrastructure investments."
  • "We now expect to exceed $2.2 billion of capital investment from 2024 through 2028" and said the company will provide on the February 2027 full-year 2026 earnings call "2027 through 2031 capital expenditure guidance" and "2027 through 2031 earnings growth rate," according to (President, CEO & Chairman Householder).
  • "Adjusted gross margin was approximately $150 million" and "adjusted net income was approximately $25 million," while "adjusted earnings per share were $1.05," said (Senior VP & CFO Jeffrey S. Sylvester). He said the EPS result "is reflective of the shares we've issued throughout the last year as we return to our target capital structure."

Outlook

  • "We are updating" the five-year capital range and "now expect to exceed $2.2 billion of capital investment from 2024 through 2028," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder), and added, "we now expect to provide" in February 2027 "2027 through 2031" capital guidance and "earnings growth rate."
  • "We remain committed" and are "reaffirming our 2028 earnings per share guidance of $7.75 to $8," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester).
  • Compared with last quarter’s messaging about revisiting the capital range by February 2027, management tied the timing and scope more directly to FEP, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying progress "particularly with the announcement of FEP, will necessitate a more fulsome update of our long-term performance expectations."

Financial results

  • "Ongoing and recently completed natural gas transmission expansion projects contributed $0.15 of adjusted earnings per share" and "margin from our infrastructure program investments accounted for an additional $0.10 per share," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester). He also cited "$0.06 of incremental adjusted EPS" from distribution demand and "$0.06 of improved propane and Aspire performance."
  • Offsets included "$0.04" tied to "consumption, quarterly timing differences and other items" and "$0.04 from decreased CNG, RNG and LNG services," plus expense items including "$0.11 of increased depreciation, amortization and property tax" and "financing activity... reduced adjusted EPS by $0.05," according to (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester).
  • Balance sheet and liquidity actions included: "we have just completed an amendment of our revolving credit agreement, bringing the total borrowing capacity under the revolver to $650 million, an increase of $200 million," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester), and noted "70% of our total debt capacity of $798 million available" as of June 30.

Q&A

  • Constantine Lednev, Wells Fargo: asked about FEP regulatory/permitting, shipper interest, upsizing, and how it fits the February update; (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) responded, "we do expect there's growth in that potential project" and "we expect to have" the partnership "aligned here in the quarter," while (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said it is "jurisdictional to the Florida Public Service Commission" and that the route will be "largely in the public right of way" with permitting expected "to go relatively smoothly for a project of this size."
  • Lednev, Wells Fargo: asked why use a partner and about funding structures; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said partnering helps "maintain a reasonable balance on the risk" and reflects managing earnings while building "capital up to about $600 million on our side of the project" before revenue begins in 2030.
  • Michael Brown, Barclays: asked whether there is common ground for a Florida City Gas (FCG) rate-case settlement; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I don't know that we will get to a settlement... and we're certainly prepared to fully litigate it if we need to."
  • Brown, Barclays: asked about EPS guidance for 2027 and beyond 2028; (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) said, "We're not signaling it here" but will provide "more clarity" on "the five-year growth rate and the capital" in February 2027.
  • Tate Sullivan, Maxim: asked about FEP timing and whether it is the first intrastate partnership; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said capacity shortfalls were recognized "back in the mid-'90s" and that it will be the first: "Yes, that's exactly right. It is."
  • Sullivan, Maxim: asked about potential WRU expansion approvals; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I'd like to think that it's a given. I never assume that," adding that LNG facilities are "the least expensive way and most efficient way" to meet Delmarva demand.
  • Christopher Ellinghaus, Siebert: asked about Virginia feasibility and Canaveral; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said Accomack work is "beginning the feasibility analysis" and Canaveral requires securing property, adding, "we think there's a real opportunity... and we're going to continue to be pretty aggressive." Ellinghaus also asked about broader customer-growth slowing; Householder replied, "Yes. I mean we are seeing some slowdown" but "nothing alarming to us at this point."
  • Paul Fremont, Ladenburg: asked how management will present a longer-term growth rate with a "lumpy" FEP profile; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I'm not sure we've settled on exactly how to tell that story yet," but investors should expect "at least some visibility across the five years."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical around regulatory outcomes and long-range earnings visibility, highlighted by questions on settlement prospects and longer-term EPS framing; (Barclays’ Brown) asked directly if there is "a common ground for a settlement" and pressed for EPS guidance beyond 2028.
  • Management’s tone in prepared remarks was positive and expansion-focused, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) calling FEP "a valuable long-term regulated growth opportunity" and (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) saying, "I remain highly confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results." In Q&A, responses were more cautious on uncertainty, including (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying, "I don't know that we will get to a settlement" and "I'm not sure we've settled on exactly how to tell that story yet."
  • Versus last quarter’s transition-focused tone (retiring CFO and incoming CFO), this call’s tone centered more on execution and scale, particularly the "largest single project" announcement and the expanded capital plan.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Strategic focus shifted from evaluating South Florida capacity options in Q1 to announcing FEP in Q2, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) describing FEP as a committed, shipper-anchored project expected in service in 2030.
  • Capital messaging changed from Q1’s $450 million to $500 million 2026 capex range to Q2’s "updated range of $550 million to $600 million," driven by FEP and broader regulated investment.
  • CFO leadership transitioned fully: Q1 introduced Jeff Sylvester as "incoming" CFO and featured outgoing CFO Beth Cooper; Q2 reflected Sylvester delivering the CFO financial update.
  • Analyst questioning broadened from Q1’s equity-financing mechanics and project exploration to Q2’s emphasis on FEP permitting/partnership structure, the FCG rate case litigation risk, and how long-term growth will be communicated.

Risks and concerns

  • Regulatory risk in Florida was explicit, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying on the FCG rate case, "we're certainly prepared to fully litigate it if we need to."
  • Execution and timing risk around large capital projects was embedded in the need to manage earnings before FEP revenues, as (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) referenced building capital "to about $600 million on our side of the project" before service in 2030.
  • Demand and mix risks included "some slowdown" in customer growth (Householder) and "decreased CNG, RNG and LNG services" (Sylvester), alongside expense pressure items such as higher depreciation, insurance, and customer-related costs (Sylvester).

Final takeaway

Management presented Q2 as a step-up in scale and long-duration visibility, anchored by the newly announced $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project targeted for 2030 in-service, alongside a $100 million increase to 2026 capex guidance and a plan to refresh multi-year capital and growth-rate disclosures in February 2027. The call also underscored near-term uncertainty around the Florida City Gas rate case, with management indicating it may proceed without settlement, while reiterating 2028 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.75 to $8 and highlighting ongoing financing capacity expansion through a larger revolving credit facility.

data.title: Tech stocks take off as earnings results, powered up by AI deals, propel market higher
data.description:
A wide range of technology and AI-exposed stocks were climbing on Friday, supported by a deep list of strong earnings results reported during the week.

For example, indie Semiconductor (INDI) shares had surged more than 15% by noon trading following its second quarter results. Meanwhile, Corsair Gaming (CRSR) rocketed more than 30% after reporting its second quarter results and outlook.

Five9 (FIVN) jumped more than 15% after it forecasted AI-related revenue to increase by at least 60% year over year for 2026.

"AI revenue grew 78% year-on-year, and we are increasing our full-year AI growth outlook from more than 40% to at least 60% year-on-year," said Five9 CEO Amit Mathradas.

He explained in detail how AI has strengthened, not disrupted, Five9's software platform.

"Contact centers are going through a major transformation," Mathradas said during Thursday's earnings call. "Service is no longer viewed only as a cost center to contain. Increasingly, enterprises see customer experience as a lever for loyalty, retention and growth. They want to resolve more issues, respond faster, personalize more interactions and create better outcomes for customers at scale. AI is enabling that shift by automating routine work and improving the economics of service. In many customer conversations, the ROI is becoming clearer, better service, more capacity, faster response times and stronger customer outcomes."

Other enterprise software firms were also demonstrating how AI was benefiting their projections. Appian (APPN) shares surged 14% on Friday following its second quarter results and outlook on Thursday.

"Some companies are clearly going to benefit from AI," said Appian CEO Matt Calkins in an interview with Seeking Alpha. "We are absolutely a beneficiary of the day. It is a clear benefit for us. There is no confusion or delay. There is only acceleration and growth."

"We are a complement to AI," he added. "When you want AI to do important work, you need a deterministic layer. We provide it. We provide a suite of functionality that allows you to use AI safely and effectively. We are a boost to AI. I think what everybody can agree on is that AI needs a software counterpart."

Semiconductor and software firms were both taking part in Friday's rally, as evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) increasing by 2% and 3%, respectively.

data.title: Onto Innovation stock jumps 13% on $1.1B backlog, upbeat outlook, AI demand
data.description:
Onto Innovation (ONTO) stock jumped over ~13% to ~$306 on Friday after the company reported a strong set of Q2 earnings and gave an optimistic outlook for the coming quarters. The rally pushed the stock's gain for the week to nearly 23%.

Moreover, the stock has been one of the best performers in the semiconductor sector this year, gaining 96.61% year to date, compared with the S&P 500 (SP500)'s 12.63% return in the same period.

The biggest reason behind Onto Innovation's price surge was a record second quarter with a revenue of $343.1M, up 35% from a year ago, while non-GAAP earnings rose to $1.93 per share from $1.25 last year.

The company said revenue, profit margins, and earnings all came in above the high end of its guidance.

Growth was driven by strong demand for AI-related semiconductor technologies. Revenue from advanced nodes jumped 50% from the previous quarter, while advanced packaging and specialty devices also reached record levels, supported by demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), 2.5D packaging, and silicon photonics.

Investors were also encouraged by the company's record backlog of more than $1.1B, providing better visibility into future sales.

Looking ahead, Onto Innovation expects Q3 revenue of $380M-$400M and non-GAAP EPS of $2.18-$2.38. Management also raised its second-half revenue growth outlook to 25% or more, saying strong AI demand could continue well into 2027.

The company also enjoys strong support from analysts. Wall Street has a 'Strong Buy' rating, while Seeking Alpha and the Quant system rate the stock 'Buy,' reflecting confidence in the company's growth outlook.
